newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: SE Asia Grains - Malaysia, Thailand buy corn.
newsitem.headline: SE Asia Grains - Malaysia, Thailand buy corn.

text.p: Malaysia and Thailand are said to have bought up to 80,000 tonnes of Chinese and Argentine corn in the past two weeks. Indonesia may also be looking to pick up more corn from China, traders said on Wednesday.

A major flour mill in Thailand was reported to have purchased 50,000 tonnes of corn from Argentina for March shipment, dealers said. The Malaysians were estimated to have bought some 30,000 tonnes of Chinese corn.
Malaysian traders said several flour mills and general maize importers had purchased the Chinese corn at around US$150 a tonne C&F, ex-godown in the central region.
"There were several buyers, but nobody was buying big," a Singapore trader who monitors the Malaysian market said. "It was all for around 10 or 20 tonnes each, more for shortcovering."
"There was no panic buying...most of the orders have been locked for April/May," the purchasing manager for a flour mill in Kuala Lumpur added.
One Singapore dealer estimated the amount of corn bought by Malaysia from China to range between 20,000 to 30,000 tonnes.
In Thailand, the flour mill involved in buying corn from Argentina apparently believes the government has finalised its zero-tariff scheme for corn imports.
"The buyer might expect that the government will have already come up with details on zero-tariff corn imports by the time the shipments arrive in May or June," one Thai trader said.
Corn prices in Thailand and Indonesia have recently firmed on brisk demand, while easing slightly in Malaysia.
Indonesian dealers said corn was quoted at 410-415 rupiah a kg in Jakarta, against 400-410 rupiah a kg last week.
"Local corn prices have been considerably up as demand from feedmills has also risen," one trader in Jakarta said.
"Indonesia has bought 100,000 tonnes of Chinese corn and buyers are looking for more," another dealer said.
The trader said the buying spree seemed to indicate that people in Indonesia were not very optimistic about the prospects for local corn production.
"Everybody is buying, but there is no reason for the people to buy unless they know for sure there's not much local corn available," he said.
Other traders believe the feedmills are engaged in some purchases merely to take some positions in the market, adding that local stocks were sufficient.

The Indonesian traders said U.S. corn was quoted at $142-$143 a tonne C&F on a Panamax, against $145 a tonne last week, while Handy-sized cargoes were quoted at $150 a tonne C&F against $153 a tonne in the previous week.
In Thailand, the domestic corn price edged up this week to 4.40 baht a kg from 4.25 baht last week because of improved demand, trade sources said.
The price of bulk corn, ex-factory/godown in Malaysia's central region, was at between 400-415 ringgit a tonne, compared to 420-430 ringgit a week ago.
Traders attributed the lower Malaysian prices to the assurance of stable supply from China.
"The Chicago Board's corn prices may have jumped but the Chinese have maintained their price, probably due to their sufficent supply," said a Malaysian-based trader.
In the soymeal market, Thailand is seen engaging in some modest buying for May shipment, dealers said.
"The total buying since last week could be around a cargo or so. Those who bought seemed to believe that the price could edge up further," a U.S. commodity house trader said.

"But those who remained sidelined think prices are still too expensive and should come down further. With local output coming to the market soon, I guess they think they can afford to wait," he added.
Thai soymeal was quoted slightly higher at 9.65 baht a kg from 9.60 baht last week.

U.S. soymeal for May/June delivery was indicated at $360 a tonne C&F while Indian meal was seen at $338-$340 a tonne C&F. South American meal was quoted at $325-$340 a tonne C&F, depending on the grade.
Indonesian dealers, on the other hand, said soymeal prices were higher on steady demand. Soymeal was quoted at 830 rupiah a kg, against 810-820 last week.
One trader said Indian soymeal was quoted at $326 a tonne C&F, unchanged from last week.
In Malaysia, soymeal prices were seen at 850 ringgit a tonne for the local material and 845 ringgit for imported soymeal against 890 and 870 ringgit, respectively, last week.
Grade "A" wheat in bags, ex-factory/godown in the central region, was 100 ringgit higher at 850 ringgit a tonne. The local wheat was 50 ringgit higher at 500 ringgit a tonne.
